import pandas as pd

# Source file paths
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_12/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_12/training_1.csv"

# Load Source 0: School info table
# Columns: ['School ID', 'school_name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
# index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df_source0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)

# Load Source 1: Student scores table
# Columns: ['Student ID', 'student_name', 'gender', 'grade', 'school_name', 'reading_score', 'math_score']
df_source1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)

# Transformation plan:
# Target schema: ['school_name': string, 'reading_score': integer]
# Target examples show aggregated reading_score per school_name (e.g. Figueroa High School 2949)
# Source0 has school_name and school attributes but no reading_score
# Source1 has school_name and reading_score per student
# So we need to aggregate reading_score by school_name from Source1
# Then join with Source0 on school_name to ensure all schools from Source0 are included if needed
# But target examples only show school_name and reading_score, so we only need to aggregate reading_score by school_name from Source1
# Source0 is not needed for aggregation but prompt says all source tables must be used
# So we will join aggregated reading_score from Source1 with Source0 on school_name to ensure all schools from Source0 are represented
# For schools in Source0 but not in Source1, reading_score will be NaN, fill with 0 or drop? Target examples show only schools with reading_score > 0
# We will keep only schools that have reading_score > 0 after aggregation (inner join)
# Finally, select columns ['school_name', 'reading_score'] and convert reading_score to int

# Aggregate reading_score by school_name from Source1
agg_scores = df_source1.groupby('school_name', as_index=False)['reading_score'].sum()

# Join aggregated scores with Source0 on school_name to ensure all schools from Source0 are considered
# Use inner join to keep only schools present in both (since target examples show only schools with reading_score)
df_joined = pd.merge(df_source0[['school_name']], agg_scores, on='school_name', how='inner')

# Ensure reading_score is integer type
df_joined['reading_score'] = df_joined['reading_score'].astype(int)

# Select final columns as per target schema
df_target = df_joined[['school_name', 'reading_score']]

# Write the result to the specified path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length2_12/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
